claims.text: The starting material is a nominally homogeneous high-entropy alloy containing five or more uniformly mixed elements.
The starting alloy is chemically disordered.
Controlled thermal annealing can promote subtle short-range chemical ordering or clustering in the alloy.
Nb and Ti are high-electron–phonon-coupling elements relevant to the proposed alloy.
Annealing will create local clusters or compositional microdomains enriched in Nb and Ti.
Nb- and Ti-enriched microdomains will have a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The increased local density of states will enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling will enable Cooper pairing and an observable superconducting transition.
A low-temperature test regime below approximately 10 K is appropriate based on analogous high-entropy superconductors.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate under ambient pressure.
Relative to the disordered baseline, the annealed alloy should display a superconducting transition at a higher critical temperature or with greater superconducting robustness.
A superconducting transition can be observed through a resistivity drop and a specific-heat jump.
Rapid quenching retains a homogeneous, disordered baseline state without significant local elemental enrichment.
The disordered baseline should exhibit no superconducting signal or only a weak one.
The mechanism requires the concentration of high-electron–phonon-coupling elements to exceed a threshold.
The mechanism applies only when short-range ordering occurs without compromising the overall high-entropy phase.
Resistivity, magnetization, and specific heat measurements can jointly test for zero resistance, a Meissner response, and a thermodynamic anomaly at the transition.

Failure of annealed samples to show a statistically significant increase in critical temperature, specific-heat anomaly, or Meissner response relative to the baseline would falsify the proposed enhancement mechanism.
The ordering level required for superconductivity, the sensitivity of critical temperature to ordering, and the influence of disorder and scattering are uncertain.
